previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol and opioid dependence, alcoholic cirrhosis, and asthma was admitted for severe epigastric, right upper quadrant, and left upper quadrant abdominal pain following a relapse involving a pint of hard alcohol. The pain, radiating to the back and worsened by meals, was consistent with acute alcoholic hepatitis and chronic pancreatitis flare. He was managed supportively with IV fluids, bowel rest, and pain control, and monitored for alcohol withdrawal using CIWA without complications. Imaging showed a diffusely echogenic liver, reversal of portal vein flow, and pericholecystic fluid without gallstones. Liver enzymes and symptoms improved during the hospitalization. He expressed motivation to remain abstinent, and plans were made to restart Suboxone and arrange follow-up with hepatology and addiction services. He was discharged home with a short-term oxycodone prescription, lorazepam for anxiety, and continuation of all chronic medications.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Epigastric abdominal pain, LFT elevation, negative lipase.

COMPARISON:  Right upper quadrant ultrasound from ___.  

TECHNIQUE:  Gray scale and Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:

The liver is diffusely echogenic, with the course, nodular echotexture
consistent with fatty infiltration.  No focal lesion is identified.  Doppler
assessment of the portal vein demonstrates patency with unchanged reversal of
flow in the main and right posterior portal veins.  There is no evidence of
intra or extrahepatic biliary dilatation and the common bile duct measures 5
mm.  The gallbladder is normal without evidence of stones or gallbladder wall
thickening.  The pancreas is not well visualized due to overlying bowel gas. 
There is stable splenomegaly measuring 15.2 cm.  No ascites.  

IMPRESSION:

1. Echogenic liver consistent with fatty deposition.  Other forms of liver
disease and more advanced liver disease including significant hepatic fibrosis
or cirrhosis cannot be excluded on this study.  

2.  Reversal of flow in the main and right posterior portal veins again seen.

HISTORY:  Epigastric pain and chest pain.

unremarkable.  The hilar contours are also stable and unremarkable.
